text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Authorities' cash flows are very loosely controlled by the state, especially regional development structure funds, a study by the State Finances Inspections Bureau shows.

- Finland's EU commissioner seat is not in danger, even though Dutch proposal at Inter Governmental Conference does not mention commissioner numbers, says Eikka Kosonen, director of the Finnish EU-secretariat.
- Division of work between President and Prime Minister at EU meetings was approved unconstitutionally, professor of constitution Antero Jyranki says.

- Competition in Finnish energy markets has tightened in recent years: it shows in pricing and results - Neste will also start looking for markets in Poland and Russia, says Veli-Matti Ropponen, director of oil market functions at Neste.
- Finnish foreign net debt including interest has fallen under 200 billion markka.
- Enso CEO Jukka Harmala and Kvaerner Masa-Yards CEO Martin Saarikangas were made honorary mining councellors.
- Foreign capital in Finnish companies should be more visible, Second Finance Minister Arja Alho says.
- Some Finnish companies -- including railways, Nokia, Post and Tele - face new problems: cash reserves are too high and they have no clear investment targets.

- State companies face no risk of excessive the share option awards, says Finance and Trade Minister Antti Kalliomaki: supports share options for campany managers but admits some private companies' have damaged their reputations through it.
- Finnish economy is doing well and does not need any more help: we are staring too much at the EMU-criteria, says Kirsi Hokkanen, chief economist at Handelsbanken.
- Democracy in municipalities is diminishing, says Jacob Soderman, EU ombudsman.
